flags.title: DC Alliance — Medicaid for Undocumented Adults (Unique in Registry)
flags.summary: DC Healthcare Alliance provides Medicaid-equivalent coverage for undocumented adults — the only program of its kind in the registry. Income limit: 200% FPL. DC Health Link: 855-532-5465 / dchealthlink.com. DHCF: 202-442-5988.

flags.title: $17.50/hr Minimum Wage — Highest in Registry
flags.summary: DC's minimum wage of $17.50/hr is the highest in the entire registry. Tipped minimum: $8.00/hr. For wage claims: DC DOES: 202-671-1880 / does.dc.gov. Also file federal WHD.

flags.title: DC OHR 1-Year SOL — Broadest Protected Classes in Registry
flags.summary: DC Office of Human Rights has a 1-year SOL and the broadest set of protected classes in the registry: race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, marital status, personal appearance, sexual orientation, gender identity, familial status, family responsibilities, matriculation, political affiliation, genetic information, disability, source of income, place of residence, and homeless status. DC OHR: 202-727-4559 / ohr.dc.gov.

flags.title: Wards 7 & 8 — 25-35% Poverty vs NW DC $120k+ Median Income
flags.summary: DC has extreme income inequality. Wards 7 and 8 (east of the Anacostia River) have 25-35% poverty rates while Northwest DC has median incomes exceeding $120,000. Services in Wards 7 & 8 are limited. Bread for the City: 202-265-1234 / breadforthecity.org. Legal Aid Society of DC: 202-628-1161 / legalaiddc.org.

flags.title: No Congressional Representation — Federal Override of DC Law
flags.summary: DC residents have no voting representation in Congress. Congress can override DC laws, including budget decisions. This affects local policy stability. DC Council: 202-724-8000 / dccouncil.gov.

flags.title: Involuntary Hold: DC Emergency Hospitalization
flags.message: DC involuntary psychiatric hold law: DC Emergency Hospitalization. Statutory authority: D.C. Code § 21-521. Maximum initial hold duration: 48 hours. Legal standard: danger to self/others. A hearing must be held before the hold can be extended. The person has the right to counsel at the hearing.
action_items: Verify hold did not exceed 48 hours without court order
Confirm hearing was held within statutory timeframe
Check that patient rights notice was provided at admission
Request complete hold documentation from facility

flags.title: Psychiatric Patient Rights
flags.message: Psychiatric patients in DC retain fundamental rights during hospitalization: right to communicate with persons outside the facility, right to receive and send mail, right to access legal counsel, right to refuse treatment (with limited exceptions), right to informed consent, right to access medical records, and right to file grievances. These rights cannot be restricted as a condition of treatment.
action_items: Verify patient rights notice was provided and signed
Check whether any rights were restricted and if proper procedures were followed
Confirm access to legal counsel was not impeded

flags.title: Federal Restraint & Seclusion Limits
flags.message: Federal law (42 CFR § 482.13) sets strict limits on restraint and seclusion in DC: physician order required within 1 hour, face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour, continuous monitoring required, maximum 4 hours per order for adults (2 hours for ages 9-17, 1 hour for under 9), and restraint may only be used to protect the patient from harm — never as punishment, convenience, or retaliation.
action_items: Request restraint/seclusion logs for all episodes
Verify physician order was obtained within 1 hour
Check that face-to-face evaluation occurred within 1 hour
Verify restraint was not used as punishment or convenience
Check for injuries during restraint episodes
legal_references: CMS State Operations Manual Appendix A

flags.title: Involuntary Psychiatric Hold Statute
flags.message: This state has specific statutes governing involuntary psychiatric holds. Know the time limits, hearing rights, and appeal procedures before they expire.
flags.statute: District of Columbia Involuntary Commitment Act

flags.title: Mental Health Patient Bill of Rights
flags.message: This state has a Patient Bill of Rights for mental health facilities. Facilities must inform patients of these rights upon admission.
flags.statute: District of Columbia Mental Health Patient Rights Act

flags.title: Discharge Planning Requirements
flags.message: This state requires facilities to create discharge plans with follow-up appointments, medication management, and community resource referrals.
flags.statute: District of Columbia Mental Health Discharge Planning Standards
